passages.text: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the temple courts.
He was teaching the people.
He was proclaiming the gospel.
The chief priests came to Him.
The scribes came to Him.
The elders came with them.
They all approached Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν διδάσκοντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λαὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εὐαγγελιζομένου ἐπέστησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς σὺν τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις

passages.text: “Tell us,” they said, “by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests, scribes, and elders came to Jesus.
They spoke to Jesus directly.
They said, “Tell us something.”
They asked, “By what authority do you do these things?”
They also asked, “Who gave you this authority?”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπαν λέγοντες πρὸς αὐτόν Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς ἢ τίς ἐστιν ὁ δούς σοι τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην

passages.text: “I will also ask you a question,” Jesus replied. “Tell Me: John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was teaching the people in the temple.
He was proclaiming the gospel.
The chief priests, scribes, and elders came to Jesus.
They questioned His authority.
Jesus replied to them.
He said, “I will ask you a question.”
He said, “Tell Me this.”
He said, “Was John’s baptism from heaven?”
He said, “Or was it from men?”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον καὶ εἴπατέ μοι Τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
passages.sermon:
The religious leaders spoke to each other.
They discussed what to answer Jesus.
They said, “If we say, ‘John’s baptism was from heaven,’ Jesus will ask us a question.”
He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe John?’
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ συνελογίσαντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐρεῖ Διὰ τί οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ

passages.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
passages.sermon: If we say, 'John's baptism was from men,' the people will stone us.\r\nAll the people believe John is a prophet.\r\nThey are convinced John is a prophet.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ὁ λαὸς ἅπας καταλιθάσει ἡμᾶς πεπεισμένος γάρ ἐστιν Ἰωάννην προφήτην εἶναι

passages.text: So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
passages.sermon: The people answered Jesus.\r\nThey said they did not know where it was from.\r\nThey did not give an answer about the source.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν μὴ εἰδέναι πόθεν

passages.text: And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to them.\r\nHe said, “I will not tell you by what authority I do these things.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ

passages.text: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a parable.
A man planted a vineyard.
He rented the vineyard to some tenants.
The man went away for a long time.
passages.original: Ἤρξατο δὲ πρὸς τὸν λαὸν λέγειν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην Ἄνθρωπος τις ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν χρόνους ἱκανούς

passages.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.
passages.sermon:
A man owned a vineyard.
He rented the vineyard to some tenants.
He went away for a long time.
At harvest time, the man sent a servant to the tenants.
The servant went to collect the man's share of the fruit from the vineyard.
The tenants beat the servant.
The tenants sent the servant away.
The servant returned with nothing.
passages.original: καὶ καιρῷ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς δοῦλον ἵνα ἀπὸ τοῦ καρποῦ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος δώσουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν δείραντες κενόν

passages.text: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.
passages.sermon:
The owner sent another servant.
The tenants beat this servant.
The tenants treated him shamefully.
The tenants sent him away with nothing.
passages.original: Καὶ προσέθετο ἕτερον πέμψαι δοῦλον οἱ δὲ κἀκεῖνον δείραντες καὶ ἀτιμάσαντες ἐξαπέστειλαν κενόν

passages.text: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.
passages.sermon: The owner of the vineyard sent a third servant.\r\nThe tenants wounded this servant.\r\nThe tenants threw him out.
passages.original: Καὶ προσέθετο τρίτον πέμψαι οἱ δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τραυματίσαντες ἐξέβαλον

passages.text: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.’
passages.sermon:
The owner of the vineyard spoke.
He asked, "What shall I do?"
He said, "I will send my beloved son."
He thought, "Perhaps they will respect him."
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος Τί ποιήσω πέμψω τὸν υἱόν μου τὸν ἀγαπητόν ἴσως τοῦτον ἐντραπήσονται

passages.text: But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
passages.sermon:
The tenants saw the son.
They talked to each other.
They said, "This is the heir."
They said, "Let us kill him."
They said, "Then the inheritance will belong to us."
passages.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γεωργοὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν ἵνα ἡμῶν γένηται ἡ κληρονομία

passages.text: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
passages.sermon:
The tenants threw the son out of the vineyard.
They killed him.
The owner of the vineyard saw what they did.
What will the owner do to these tenants?
passages.original: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ἀπέκτειναν Τί οὖν ποιήσει αὐτοῖς ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος

passages.text: He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.” And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!”
passages.sermon:
The owner of the vineyard will come.
He will kill those tenants.
He will give the vineyard to other people.
The people heard this.
They said, "May such a thing never happen!"
passages.original: ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργοὺς τούτους καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις Ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἶπαν Μὴ γένοιτο

passages.text: But Jesus looked directly at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the people.
Jesus looked directly at them.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus referred to a written scripture.
Jesus said, “What does this mean?”
The scripture says, “The builders rejected a stone.”
That stone became the cornerstone.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς εἶπεν Τί οὖν ἐστιν τὸ γεγραμμένον τοῦτο Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες Οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας

passages.text: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke about Himself as the stone.\r\nHe said, "Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces."\r\nHe also said, "If this stone falls on anyone, it will crush that person."
passages.original: Πᾶς ὁ πεσὼν ἐπ’ ἐκεῖνον τὸν λίθον συνθλασθήσεται ἐφ’ ὃν δ’ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν

passages.text: When the scribes and chief priests realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, they sought to arrest Him that very hour. But they were afraid of the people.
passages.sermon:
The scribes and the chief priests heard Jesus speak a parable.
They understood that Jesus spoke this parable against them.
They wanted to arrest Jesus immediately.
They feared the people.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐζήτησαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐπιβαλεῖν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν λαόν ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην

passages.text: So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
passages.sermon:
The scribes and chief priests watched Jesus closely.
They sent spies to Jesus.
These spies pretended to be sincere.
The spies acted as if they were righteous.
The scribes and chief priests wanted to catch Jesus in something He said.
They hoped to trap Jesus by His own words.
They wanted to hand Jesus over to the governor’s rule and authority.
passages.original: Καὶ παρατηρήσαντες ἀπέστειλαν ἐνκαθέτους ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου ὥστε παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν τῇ ἀρχῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος

passages.text: “Teacher,” they inquired, “we know that You speak and teach correctly. You show no partiality, but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.
passages.sermon:
The scribes and chief priests sent spies to Jesus.
The spies pretended to be sincere.
The spies spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Teacher, we know you speak correctly.
We know you teach correctly.
You do not show partiality.
You teach the way of God.
You teach according to the truth.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὀρθῶς λέγεις καὶ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ λαμβάνεις πρόσωπον ἀλλ’ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ διδάσκεις

passages.text: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
passages.sermon:
Some men came to Jesus.
These men were spies.
They pretended to be sincere.
They wanted to trap Jesus with His words.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar?”
They also asked, “Or is it not lawful?”
passages.original: ἔξεστιν ἡμᾶς Καίσαρι φόρον δοῦναι ἢ οὔ

passages.text: But Jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them, “Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw their trickery.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Show Me a denarius.”
He asked, “Whose image is on it?”
He also asked, “Whose inscription is on it?”
They answered, “Caesar’s.”
passages.original: Κατανοήσας δὲ αὐτῶν τὴν πανουργίαν εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Δείξατέ μοι δηνάριον τίνος ἔχει εἰκόνα καὶ ἐπιγραφήν Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Καίσαρος

passages.text: So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus is a teacher.
Jesus saw their question about paying taxes to Caesar.
Jesus said, “Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar.
Give to God what belongs to God.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τοίνυν ἀπόδοτε τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people; and amazed at His answer, they fell silent.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Some men tried to trap Jesus with His own words.
They could not trap Him.
The people listened.
The men heard Jesus’ answer.
They were amazed at His answer.
They became silent.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἐπιλαβέσθαι αὐτοῦ ῥήματος ἐναντίον τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ θαυμάσαντες ἐπὶ τῇ ἀποκρίσει αὐτοῦ ἐσίγησαν

passages.text: Then some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to question Him.
passages.sermon: Some Sadducees came to Jesus.\r\nThe Sadducees say there is no resurrection.\r\nThey questioned Jesus.
passages.original: Προσελθόντες δέ τινες τῶν Σαδδουκαίων οἱ ἀντιλέγοντες ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν

passages.text: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.
passages.sermon:
Some of the Sadducees came to Jesus.
The Sadducees did not believe in the resurrection.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, "Teacher, Moses wrote a law for us."
Moses said, "If a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the brother must marry the widow."
The brother must have children with her for his dead brother.
This law helps the dead brother have descendants.
passages.original: λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ ἔχων γυναῖκα καὶ οὗτος ἄτεκνος ᾖ ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married a wife, but died childless.
passages.sermon:
There were seven brothers.
The first brother married a wife.
He died.
He had no children.
passages.original: ἑπτὰ οὖν ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν καὶ ὁ πρῶτος λαβὼν γυναῖκα ἀπέθανεν ἄτεκνος

passages.text: Then the second and the third married the widow, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
passages.sermon:
The second brother married the widow.
The third brother also married her.
All seven brothers married her in the same way.
None of the brothers had children with her.
All seven brothers died.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐ κατέλιπον τέκνα καὶ ἀπέθανον

passages.text: And last of all, the woman died.
passages.sermon: The woman lived after the seven brothers died.\r\nShe died last.
passages.original: ὕστερον καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν

passages.text: So then, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”
passages.sermon:
Seven brothers each married the same woman.
\r\nEach brother died.
\r\nNone of them had children with her.
\r\nLater, the woman also died.
\r\nPeople asked about the resurrection.
\r\nThey asked, "Whose wife will she be in the resurrection?"
\r\nAll seven brothers had married her.
passages.original: ἡ γυνὴ οὖν ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τίνος αὐτῶν γίνεται γυνή οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα

passages.text: Jesus answered, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He answered their question.
He said, “People in this world marry.
People in this world are given in marriage.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου γαμοῦσιν καὶ γαμίσκονται

passages.text: But those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
passages.sermon:
Some people will be considered worthy by God.
These people will take part in the age to come.
These people will also take part in the resurrection from the dead.
These people will not marry.
Others will not give them in marriage.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ καταξιωθέντες τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐκείνου τυχεῖν καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται

passages.text: In fact, they can no longer die, because they are like the angels. And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.
passages.sermon:
Those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead cannot die anymore.
They are like the angels.
They are sons of God.
They are sons of the resurrection.
passages.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀποθανεῖν ἔτι δύνανται ἰσάγγελοι γάρ εἰσιν καὶ υἱοί εἰσιν Θεοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως υἱοὶ ὄντες

passages.text: Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet of God.
Moses spoke to God at the burning bush.
Moses showed that God raises the dead.
Moses called the Lord “the God of Abraham.”
Moses called the Lord “the God of Isaac.”
Moses called the Lord “the God of Jacob.”
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had died long before Moses.
Moses still called God their God.
This shows that the dead are raised.
passages.original: Ὅτι δὲ ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροὶ καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐμήνυσεν ἐπὶ τῆς Βάτου ὡς λέγει Κύριον Τὸν Θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Θεὸν Ἰακώβ

passages.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.”
passages.sermon: God is not the God of the dead.\r\nGod is the God of the living.\r\nAll people are alive to God.
passages.original: Θεὸς δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν

passages.text: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, You have spoken well!”
passages.sermon: Some scribes listened to Jesus.\r\nThese scribes answered Jesus.\r\nThey said, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθέντες δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν Διδάσκαλε καλῶς εἶπας

passages.text: And they did not dare to question Him any further.
passages.sermon:
The scribes listened to Jesus.
They did not ask Him any more questions.
They did not have the courage to question Him again.
They stopped questioning Jesus.
passages.original: οὐκέτι γὰρ ἐτόλμων ἐπερωτᾶν αὐτὸν οὐδέν

passages.text: Then Jesus declared, “How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David?
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to them.\r\nJesus asked a question.\r\nHe said, “How can people say that the Christ is the Son of David?”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Πῶς λέγουσιν τὸν Χριστὸν εἶναι Δαυὶδ υἱόν

passages.text: For David himself says in the book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” ’
passages.sermon:
David was a king of Israel.
David wrote many psalms.
David speaks in the book of Psalms.
David says, “The Lord said to my Lord.”
God speaks to David’s Lord.
God says, “Sit at My right hand.”
God says, “Stay there until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
passages.original: αὐτὸς γὰρ Δαυὶδ λέγει ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν Εἶπεν Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου Ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου Ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου

passages.text: Thus David calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?”
passages.sermon: David calls Him Lord.\r\nHow can He be David’s son?
passages.original: Δαυὶδ οὖν αὐτὸν Κύριον καλεῖ καὶ πῶς αὐτοῦ υἱός ἐστιν

passages.text: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples, “Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
All the people were listening.
Jesus warned them about the scribes.
The scribes like to walk around in long robes.
They love to receive greetings in the marketplaces.
They want the best seats in the synagogues.
They want the places of honor at banquets.
passages.original: Ἀκούοντος δὲ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων περιπατεῖν ἐν στολαῖς καὶ φιλούντων ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις

passages.text: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the scribes.
The scribes take away the houses of widows.
They pretend to be holy by making long prayers in public.
They do this only to be seen by others.
God will judge these men more strictly.
They will receive greater condemnation.
passages.original: οἳ κατεσθίουσιν τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσεύχονται οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα
